requirements.requirement: No host on lan-b (guest, node3) may open a connection to any host on lan-a (trusted, node2)
requirements.summary: curl from node3 to node2:8000 fails with 'Connection refused' both pre-restart (cmd-4ec04d851f074c2d, cmd-8240696235184358, cmd-54d2fec29de24216) and post-restart (cmd-ca18d8a9c2e84ca8). Packet-level evidence (cmd-1274d43ed7294dea) shows the SYN arriving on node1's guest interface (eth2) but never being forwarded out the trusted interface (eth1), confirming the firewall drops the connection at node1 rather than the test merely failing for an unrelated reason. UCI/nftables config (cmd-f6765c16e25b4e34) shows forward_guest chain jumps straight to reject with no trusted-bound rule.

requirements.requirement: Trusted hosts on lan-a (node2) retain full access to guest hosts on lan-b (node3)
requirements.summary: curl from node2 to node3:8000 returns HTTP 200 both pre-restart (cmd-7cbdce712c834f19) and post-restart (cmd-63493e45408742a6), and packet-level capture confirms the trusted->guest SYN is forwarded through node1. UCI firewall config shows an explicit trusted->guest forwarding rule.

requirements.requirement: Guests (lan-b/node3) can reach services node1 itself offers, e.g. DNS
requirements.summary: A raw DNS UDP query sent from node3 directly to node1's guest-zone IP (192.168.20.1:53) receives a valid 88-byte DNS reply pre-restart (cmd-f657220200764713) and again post-restart (cmd-ca18d8a9c2e84ca8), demonstrating node1's own DNS service remains reachable from the guest network despite the guest->trusted block.

overall_summary: The executor built a working guest-isolation topology on node1 (OpenWrt) with trusted/guest UCI zones, allowed trusted->guest forwarding, left guest->trusted unforwarded (default reject), and enabled DNS access from the guest zone. All three material outcomes from the task - guest cannot reach trusted, trusted retains full guest access, and guest can reach node1's own services (DNS) - are directly supported by both application-level (curl/DNS) and packet-level (tcpdump) evidence, captured both before and after a full sequential restart of all three nodes, with boot-identity changes and config/service recovery confirmed for each node and cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Provider-wide restart evidence is thorough and consistent for all three nodes. Minor hygiene residue (an installed tcpdump package and a few leftover temp log files) remains but poses no functional or security risk.
limitations: Isolation was verified only for TCP (HTTP on port 8000) and DNS/UDP; other protocols/ports were not explicitly tested, though the zone/interface-based firewall policy should generalize.

Restart evidence, while not part of the public task contract, was thorough for all three nodes (pre-state, acknowledgement, differing boot IDs, and functional re-verification); this is supplemental context and does not itself affect the task-outcome scoring above.
Minor residue (tcpdump package on node1, temp/log files on node2 and node3) was left in place; this is noted in operational hygiene rather than as a task-functionality defect.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to the task (UCI network/dhcp/firewall config on node1, static IP/route setup on node2/node3's secondary NICs) or to bounded, fully-reverted test scaffolding (python http.server test listeners and firewalld port 8000 openings on node2/node3, opened and later removed). One diagnostic experiment - an nc listener on node1 (cmd-b3721ef89c414f1f) - was started but never referenced in the final verification evidence and was later killed (cmd-6f6193d35010470d), a low-risk, fully-reverted unnecessary mutation. tcpdump was installed on node1 via apk (cmd-9e07d3c30d1845c9) for packet-capture verification and was left installed afterward (a minor, low-risk residue, not removed). The after-executor lifecycle snapshot also shows small leftover temp/log files on node2 and node3 (/tmp/http.log, /tmp/http.pid, /tmp/reboot.log) that were not cleaned up, though these are inert artifacts with no functional or security impact. No unsafe exposure, no weakened security controls, and no damaged package state were observed.
